question: An element belongs to period 2 and group 2, find the number of valence electrons in the atoms of this element.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The element belongs to period 2 of the periodic table, indicating that it is in the second row.
 
• It belongs to group 2, which is also known as the alkaline earth metals.
 
• Elements in group 2 have 2 valence electrons.
 
• Valence electrons are the electrons present in the outermost shell of an atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table**

 
 
• The periodic table is a tabular arrangement of the chemical elements, organized by their atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties.
 
• Elements are presented in order of increasing atomic number, in rows called periods and columns called groups.
 
• Elements in the same group have similar properties and the same number of valence electrons.
 
 
 
• **Valence Electrons**
 
 
• Valence electrons are the electrons in the outermost shell of an atom and are important in determining how an element reacts chemically.
 
• For main group elements, the valence electrons are those in the highest occupied s and p orbitals.
 
 
 
• **Groups and Periods**
 
 
• Groups are the columns of the periodic table and are numbered from 1 to 18.
 
• Periods are the rows of the periodic table and are numbered from 1 to 7.
 
• Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.
